s1.explanation: The unit responds to a single real, full-size road vehicle (car, pickup, van, truck) shown whole from a side or three-quarter view, with its body, windshield/cab and wheels clearly outlined and parked on pavement. It responds most to classic and red vehicles (red pickup, fire engine, red station wagon). Activity drops for interior views, toys, front-on close-ups, cluttered scenes with several vehicles or people, and odd vehicle types such as tractors. Unlike the similar units, it stays strong for boxy cab vehicles (fire engine, snowplow truck, locomotive cab, police van) and is weak for tractors and for convertibles full of people.

s2.explanation: The unit responds to the exterior body of a single real road vehicle (car, pickup, ambulance or fire truck) seen whole from the side or three-quarter front, with the hood, cab windshield and side windows clearly outlined. It is strongest for boxy or classic vehicles, often red, parked on pavement. It is weak for interiors and cargo areas, toy models, tractors and other farm-style machines, cluttered scenes with several vehicles, and photos where people dominate or cover the car. Compared with similar units, it prefers clean side-profile road vehicles such as fire engines, police vans and school buses over tractors, convertibles full of people and odd utility bodies.

s3.explanation: The unit responds to a whole, enclosed road vehicle (car, pickup, truck cab, or fire engine) seen side-on or from the front three-quarter angle, so the body side, wheels and windshield/cab are all clearly visible. It is strongest for boxy cabs with a distinct hood, such as classic pickups, fire engines and snowplow trucks. It is weaker for rear views, interiors, partial or cluttered views, scenes dominated by people, open vehicles like tractors and convertibles, and toys.

real_s1.explanation: The unit responds to a single real, whole road vehicle with an enclosed cab (car, pickup, van, truck), best when shown in side or three-quarter view. It responds less to partial views, interiors, crowded scenes, and toys or models.

real_s2.explanation: The unit most likely responds to motor vehicles in general (cars, trucks, vans, fire engines, buses), with related machines like tractors and toy vehicles also in its top classes. The specific refinements in the explanation (side view, real road vehicle, red, unobstructed by people) are not supported beyond what most units show.

real_s3.explanation: The unit responds to a single complete road vehicle (car, pickup, truck, fire engine) shown whole, wheels to roof, as the clear main subject of the photo.

null_s1.explanation: The unit responds to real, full-size road vehicles with an enclosed cab (cars, pickups, vans, trucks, including boxy ones like fire engines), most strongly when one whole vehicle is clearly shown with few prominent people. Toys, models and drawings, crowded or partial views, and people-dominated scenes give weaker responses.

null_s2.explanation: The unit responds to real full-size road vehicles (cars, trucks, vans, emergency vehicles) seen clearly and not hidden by people. It does not appear to depend on viewing angle or body color.

null_s3.explanation: The unit is most active on road-vehicle photo classes (cars, pickups, trucks, fire engines), but within those classes none of the proposed visual properties (viewing angle, completeness, people, enclosed body) explains its variation, so what drives it beyond class membership is unclear.
